newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- CLAIMS OF PUBLIC PAY SHORTFALL CHALLENGED

A new earnings survey compiled by the Office for National Statistics has undermined claims by unions that public sector workers are falling behind private sector counterparts in terms of pay. The survey found that despite the government freeze on the public sector pay bill, earnings in that sector rose by 4.2 percent in the year to April 17, slightly higher than the 4.1 percent rise for the private sector.
-- FLEMINGS CHIEF HITS OUT AT UK MARKET WATCHDOG

The chief executive of UK-based investment bank Robert Fleming, which has been rocked by revelations of massive fraud by a fund manager at the bank's east-Asian joint venture Jardine Fleming, has strongly criticised UK regulators. Chief executive John Manser claimed the bank was 'going absolutely barmy in trying to find any wrongdoing' after regulators revealed that the fund manager had diverted profitable options trades to his personal trading account.
-- BT HOPES 1 BILLION STG DEAL WILL BOOST EUROPEAN AIMS

British Telecom has formally announced its strategic alliance with French utility Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE). The move completes BT efforts to gain a foothold in each of the major European telecoms markets. BT is to invest 1.1 billion stg in CGE's Cegetel telecoms subsidiary, which aims to become the chief competitor to France telecom when Europe's telecoms markets are deregulated after January 1, 1998.
-- REGIONAL ECONOMIC DISPARITIES SET TO WIDEN

A survey published Friday from the forecasting and economic research group the Henley Centre show that central and southern England will see faster economic growth over the next five years than most of the rest of the country. The forecast high-growth districts are centred on London and a number of key motorway corridors leading into it. Two of the three areas with the worst outlook are in the north east, the other being Knowsley, Merseyside.
-- EXPORTS TO US HELP OFFSET TRADE GAP

Official figures from the Office for National Statistics have revealed that Britain's trade gap with countries outside the European Union closed to its lowest level for 15 years last month. But the figures also reported that the deficit with EU countries more than doubled in July. The August figures were helped by a fall in imports from Switzerland and Norway, and stronger exports to the US, Brazil and Saudi Arabia.
-- REGULATOR FEE RISE IRKS ELECTRICITY COMPANIES

The electricity industry regulator Offer is seeking to impose a 75 percent increase in the licence fees it charges the generating, distribution and transmission companies. Offer is hoping to raise 14.5 million stg from the companies in the 1996- 67 year, compared to 8.3 million stg in 1995-96. The increase is being attributed to the extra costs Offer has incurred in making preparations for introducing competition in the electricity supply industry by April 1998.
-- GUINNESS ADMITS MISTAKES AS PROFITS RISE 5 PERCENT

Brewing group Guinness has reported a 5 percent increase in interim pre-tax profits, to 357 million stg. Announcing the results, chairman Tony Greener admitted that the group had eroded shareholder and brand value in recent years by making poor acquisitions and cutting advertising and prices of its alcoholic drinks. Guinness is now to focus on organic growth, and will maintain premium pricing backed by a sharp increase on advertising.
-- BAe ON SHORTLIST IN CONTEST FOR STN

UK-based defence industry group British Aerospace (BAe) is one of three leading European bidders who have seen off US competitors to win through to a shortlist of possible buyers for German defence electronics company STN Atlas. STN is one of Europe's leading manufacturers of radar, sonar and heavyweight torpedoes. Also on the shortlist are German group Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa), and French group Thomson.
-- INVESCO AND AIM IN LINK-UP TALKS

UK fund management group Invesco and the privately-held US mutual fund manager AIM Management are reported to be in acquisition talks. AIM has 54 billion dollars in assets under management, and Invesco has about 14 billion dollars of funds under management in the US via a Denver-based subsidiary. A merger between the two would be one of the largest consolidations in the US mutual fund industry.
-- CELLTECH SIGNS US ANTIBODIES PATENT

Slough-based biotechnology company Celltech has been awarded a wide-ranging patent in the US that could lead to a stream of royalty income. The patent covers a way to build new human antibodies to maximise their efficacy as medicines, and Celltech expects to see an early flow of income from the patent because of several drugs owned by companies that are in the final stages of testing in the US.
